goal: A new employee of Muster AG answers one English onboarding questionnaire in Lonio. It asks each piece of information once and only when a receiving party needs it for that person. From the answers, Lonio registers the employee with Pensionskasse Muster, decides whether source tax applies and computes the full Zurich source tax tariff code, so that HR has everything it needs.
context: Today HR at Muster AG collects onboarding data itself and enters it for each receiving party. For the pension fund (Pensionskasse Muster), the insurance start date is 'the number one thing'. It depends on the first working day, and that date often changes. The fund also needs the name, date of birth, canton, civil status and, for married employees, the spouse's date of birth. To find the source tax tariff, HR works out who is subject to source tax using its own rule: anyone living abroad, and people living in Switzerland who are not Swiss, have no C permit and are not married to a Swiss national or C-permit holder living in Switzerland. HR then clicks through the Zurich tariff calculator, including the cross-border questions for Germany and Liechtenstein and the detailed questions per child. HR also wants a complete postal address and asks non-Swiss employees to bring their permit. Asking too little blocks a registration, and asking too much collects personal data no party needs (G-01). Lonio replaces this work. The employee answers once in eight fixed steps (D-047), and Lonio works out the insurance start date, the civil status and canton for the fund, whether source tax applies and the full tariff code (D-001). The sources are fictional and are treated as the truth (G-06). AHV data, IT equipment, the badge photo, how data is sent to each party and all HR screens are out of scope (G-03, G-04, D-034).

sections.title: Questionnaire flow overview
sections.purpose: Set the eight steps, their order and when each applies, how the employee saves, resumes, reviews and submits, and what happens to answers that no longer apply or need changing after submission.

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's identity and the complete home address that applies on the first working day, plus the canton the pension fund needs.

sections.title: First working day and insurance start date
sections.purpose: Ask the employee for the contractual first working day and derive the pension fund insurance start date from it.

sections.title: Civil status and spouse data
sections.purpose: Ask the civil status of every employee and the spouse's or partner's date of birth where the fund needs it, and convert the civil status to the pension fund's list and to the calculator's two groups.

sections.title: Who is subject to source tax
sections.purpose: Ask only what HR's rule needs (nationality, C permit, and the spouse's nationality, C permit and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland) to decide whether the employee is subject to source tax.

sections.title: Source tax: residence abroad and cross-border questions
sections.purpose: For employees living in Germany or Liechtenstein, ask the cross-border questions to decide between the cross-border tariff, the normal tariff and 'in principle no source tax liability' for Liechtenstein, including the separate note on the double taxation agreement.

sections.title: Source tax tariff: denomination, spouse employment and tariff code
sections.purpose: Ask the denomination, whether the spouse or partner is gainfully employed and whether the employee has children, then compute the full Zurich tariff code (letter, child digit and church-tax suffix) or the result shown when no code applies.

sections.title: Source tax tariff: children
sections.purpose: Ask one block of questions per child (no maximum, age judged on the first working day) to decide whether each child counts, whether tariff H applies and what the child digit is.
